name: Goregrind
about: Goregrind is grindcore with the politics replaced by pathology. Carcass, from Liverpool, invented it on Reek of Putrefaction and Symphonies of Sickness at the end of the 1980s: lyrics lifted from medical dictionaries, pitch-shifted vocals that gurgle rather than scream, riffs that lurch between blast beats and sickly, mid-tempo grooves, and a mix thick with low-end mud. Through the 1990s it spread via tape-trading and tiny labels, with Impetigo in Illinois adding horror-movie samples, Regurgitate in Sweden and Dead Infection in Poland stripping it to pure blast-and-gurgle, and Exhumed and Haemorrhage keeping Carcass's death-metal craft. Its tone ranges from genuinely grotesque to openly comic, and a mince and porn-grind fringe takes the joke further. It remains a small, international scene of splatter aesthetics, drum machines and limited-run vinyl.

artists.name: Carcass
artists.why: the Liverpool pathologists who invented it

albums.title: Symphonies of Sickness
albums.why: Clearer than Reek, slower in places and far more musical, the second Carcass album is where goregrind's riffs, gurgles and medical vocabulary came into focus.

albums.title: Reek of Putrefaction
albums.why: Bill Steer, Jeff Walker and Ken Owen's debut, with its collage cover and bottomless mix, is the accidental founding document of gore in extreme music.

albums.title: Ultimo Mondo Cannibale
albums.why: Horror and cannibal-film samples, Stevo's gurgle and sloppy, catchy riffs on the Illinois band's debut, the American root of the style.

albums.title: Effortless Regurgitation of Bright Red Blood
albums.why: Thirty-seven tracks of Swedish blast-and-gurgle with almost no let-up, the record that reduced goregrind to its purest formula.

albums.title: A Chapter of Accidents
albums.why: The Polish band's second album, built on lyrics about industrial and domestic accidents, is goregrind at its tightest and most relentless.

albums.title: Grume
albums.why: Spain's Haemorrhage brought actual riffs and hooks to the medical theme on a debut that owes Symphonies of Sickness everything and repays it.

albums.title: Gore Metal
albums.why: Matt Harvey's San Jose band gave the Carcass template death-metal precision and thrash speed on a Relapse debut that is the style's gateway record.

albums.title: For God Your Soul... For Me Your Flesh
albums.why: Vienna's Pungent Stench mixed Autopsy-style death metal with gore humor and groove, an early European cousin to the Carcass school.

albums.title: Putrefactive and Cadaverous Odes About Necroticism
albums.why: A Czech debut of Carcass-worshipping grind with pitch-shifted vocals and medical titles, from one of Eastern Europe's first extreme bands.

albums.title: Horror of the Zombies
albums.why: The second and last Impetigo album leaned toward death metal and Italian zombie films, with a cult following that outlasted the band.

albums.title: Surgical Disembowelment
albums.why: Raw and sloppy by the band's later standards, the debut nonetheless set the Polish school's blast-heavy, hook-free approach.

albums.title: Odour of Torture
albums.why: Groove-laden, sample-heavy and openly pornographic, the German band's only proper album founded the porngrind fringe of the style.

albums.title: Hacked Up for Barbecue
albums.why: Will Rahmer's subterranean growl, Roger Beaujard's drum machine and lengthy horror samples on the Yonkers duo's most quoted album.

albums.title: Noise-A-Go Go!!!
albums.why: Forty-odd tracks of Japanese noisecore-gore on Relapse, a record that treats goregrind as a species of noise music and sometimes a joke.

albums.title: Hymns of Indigestible Suppuration
albums.why: Dutch goregrind at its most extreme: blast beats near the limits of human drumming and vocals reduced to pitch-shifted gargle.

albums.title: Carnivorous Erection
albums.why: The Swedes' Relapse debut sharpened their production without diluting the formula, and became their best-known record.

albums.title: The Dead Shall Dead Remain
albums.why: Oakland's Impaled took the Carcass template further toward death metal, with two vocalists and Necroticism-style riffing on their debut.

albums.title: Slaughtercult
albums.why: Faster and more polished than Gore Metal, with a thrash edge and some of the band's most memorable song titles.

albums.title: Night of the Ultimate Mosh
albums.why: Swedish goregrind played with punk energy and absurdist humor, the band's Razorback debut is the comic end of the style at its most likeable.

albums.title: Teenage Giallo Grind
albums.why: Spanish gore with Italian horror-film samples and a slower, Impetigo-style lurch, a cult favorite on Razorback Records.

albums.title: Morgue Sweet Home
albums.why: The band's most tuneful and best-produced album, with Luisma's riffs closer to Carcass's Necroticism era than to grind.

albums.title: Putrefaction in Progress
albums.why: The Dutch band's final album before splitting, with a drum machine pushing tempos past anything on their earlier records.

albums.title: Left Hand Pathology
albums.why: Fifteen years after their Necrology EP, the Swedes delivered a full-length of pure Symphonies of Sickness worship, done with evident love.

albums.title: Olidous Operettas
albums.why: A pseudonymous American trio of claimed pathologists playing Carcass-style goregrind with real conviction and a Relapse budget.

note: A small style documented mostly on tiny labels and demos; years follow the first full-length pressings, and there are no landmarks here beyond the two Carcass records.
